ui.title: Can my pet eat this?
ui.subtitle: Search 500+ human foods to see if they're safe for dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, hamsters, guinea pigs, ferrets, horses, turtles and fish. Benefits, risks, symptoms, vet advice, and safer alternatives.
ui.emergencyBanner: If ingested, call your vet or the Pet Poison Helpline at 1-855-764-7661 (USA).
ui.disclaimerBody: This guide is educational — always consult your veterinarian for medical decisions, especially in emergencies.

apple.name: Apple
apple.short_answer: Generally safe when prepared plain and fed in moderation. Rich in vitamin C and fiber. Always remove the seeds and core as apple seeds contain amygdalin (cyanide).
apple.benefits: Supplies essential vitamins, minerals, and healthy hydration.
apple.risks: Digestive upset if fed in excessive portions or prepared with seasonings.
apple.symptoms: None when fed in appropriate treat portions.
apple.vet_advice: Wash thoroughly, peel/deseed if needed, and offer as an occasional treat.

faqs.question: Can my dog eat apple?
faqs.answer: For dogs, this food is rated: SAFE. Rich in vitamin C and fiber. Always remove the seeds and core as apple seeds contain amygdalin (cyanide).

faqs.question: Is apple safe for cats?
faqs.answer: For cats, this food is rated: SAFE. Cats are obligate carnivores with different nutritional needs.
